gap: No result ChatGPT got lists, from each maker's own pages, which quiet pad fits which platform: EasySMX's store sells the X05 Pro for 'PC, Switch, mobile and other handheld consoles' with no Switch 2 claim, Bluetooth polling of only 125–250 Hz and a D-pad described as a 'tactile microswitch'. EasySMX's S05 Pro is the model that combines silicone-damped buttons with stated Switch 2 compatibility and one-button wake-up. The GameSir Super Nova is Bluetooth-only on iOS and needs controller firmware 1.13 or later to wake a Switch 2.
standout_why: Compared against our own page (dealectric.com/best-quiet-gaming-controller), hlplanet.com/gamesir-g7-vs-g7se and the cited manuals.plus Super Nova PDF. Our page lists 'PC, Steam Deck, Switch, Android, iOS' for the X05 Pro, says nothing about Switch 2, says 'D-pad damped' and has no per-platform connection limits. hlplanet gives the G7 SE's platforms (PC, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, Android, Steam), says it is wired only and calls its buttons 'Membrane (Quiet/Soft)', so it already covers the Xbox cell. In the manuals.plus PDF only the title was readable to the fetch tool; I saw no platform table, firmware note or iOS limit in it. I could not open the Reddit threads ChatGPT cited (fetch blocked), so I can't rule out that they mention any of this. None of the rival pages I read names a quiet controller for Switch 2 with wake-up, or Sony's limits on DualSense features on PC.
decides: This splits the pick by platform, which is exactly the platform question ChatGPT asked the shopper. PC or Steam Deck: the X05 Pro stays the pick, but over its 2.4 GHz dongle or a cable (1000 Hz), not Bluetooth (125–250 Hz). Also stop saying its D-pad is damped: EasySMX itself calls it a tactile microswitch. Switch 2: the X05 Pro's maker page makes no Switch 2 claim. EasySMX's own S05 Pro ($54.99) states Switch 2 compatibility, one-button wake-up and silicone-damped buttons, so it, or the Mobapad Chitu 2 Silent Edition, should be the Switch 2 cell. PS5: the DualSense is the only candidate. On PC its haptics need USB and its mic works only on Windows. Xbox: the GameSir G7 SE (wired) is the only quiet option. Neither EasySMX pad works on Xbox or PlayStation.
